raw_record.standard_answer: The Na$^+$ ions will flow to the Cu/Cu$^+$ half-cell

method.method_draft: First identify from the image and text that the Cu/Cu+ half-cell is on the left and the Zn/Zn2+ half-cell is on the right, connected by a NaBr salt bridge. Use the printed reaction to see that Cu+(aq) is consumed in the Cu half-cell as Cu(s) forms, while Zn2+(aq) is produced in the Zn half-cell. Because consuming Cu+ leaves the Cu solution with excess negative nitrate charge, positive salt-bridge ions must enter that half-cell. Since the salt bridge contains NaBr, the positive ion is Na+, so Na+ flows toward the Cu/Cu+ half-cell.
